title: NEB Class 12 English — Grammar — 2024
subject: english
source: NEB Grade 12 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Rewrite as directed: (a) They are building a new bridge. (passive) (b) 'I am leaving tomorrow,' she said. (reported speech) (c) If you had studied, you ___ (pass). (complete) (d) He rarely comes late, ___? (question tag) (e) You ___ not smoke here. (modal of prohibition)
questions.solution:
(a) **A new bridge is being built.** (present continuous passive: is/are being + past participle)

(b) **She said that she was leaving the next day.** (backshift the tense; change 'tomorrow' → 'the next day')

(c) **would have passed** (third conditional: had + past participle → would have + past participle)

(d) **does he?** (the sentence is negative with 'rarely', so the tag is positive)

(e) **must** — 'You must not smoke here' expresses prohibition (prohibition may also be 'cannot').
questions.knowledgeNote: In reported speech, pronouns, tenses and time words all change together — missing any one of the three loses the mark.

questions.question: Fill in the blanks with a suitable article, preposition or tense form: (a) She is ___ honest woman. (b) I have been waiting ___ two hours. (c) By the time we arrived, the film ___ (start).
questions.solution:
(a) **an** — 'honest' begins with a vowel sound (the h is silent), so the indefinite article is 'an'.

(b) **for** — 'for' precedes a duration (two hours), whereas 'since' marks a point in time (since 2 o'clock).

(c) **had started** — the past perfect expresses an action completed before another past action ('by the time we arrived').
questions.knowledgeNote: Test the article by sound, not spelling: 'a university' (y-sound) but 'an umbrella'.

questions.question: Correct the errors: (a) One of my friend is a doctor. (b) Walking down the road, a snake bit me. (c) She is senior than me.
questions.solution:
(a) One of my **friends is** a doctor — 'one of' takes a plural noun but a singular verb.

(b) **Walking down the road, I was bitten by a snake.** The original has a dangling modifier: the participle must describe the subject of the main clause, and 'a snake' cannot be walking.

(c) She is senior **to** me — 'senior', like 'junior', 'superior' and 'inferior', takes 'to', not 'than' (Latin comparatives).
questions.knowledgeNote: Dangling modifiers are the classic error-correction item: check that the introductory participle logically belongs to the main subject.
